newsitem.title: GERMANY: German grain intervention offers remain low.
newsitem.headline: German grain intervention offers remain low.

text.p: Sales offers into German grain intervention stores in the November-May 1996/97 season continued sharply lower than in the same 95/96 period, figures from the state grain intervention board BLE showed.
Volumes by January 3 totalled 320,723 tonnes compared with 1,151,603 tonnes a year earlier.
The figure described volumes accepted, but not yet delivered to stores, by the close last Friday.
Market prices of wheat and barley benefited from export hopes although domestic EU business was slack and this discouraged intervention sales, traders said.
But feed rye sales to northern and eastern German intervention stores were up as parts of the local 1996 crop did not qualify for human consumption.
